column1: San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo - baptism act No. 1720, folio 470 (1886)
column2: *** A SEVENTH CHILD, and four grandparents in one act. *** Candido Jaime, baptised 6 July 1886, "hijo legitimo de Don Luis Lerena Lenguas y de Dona Julia Juanico, orientales". Names the paternal grandparents Don Luis and Dona Justiniana Lenguas and the maternal Don Candido and Dona Juliana Gonzalez - which CLOSES the question of who Candido Juanico's wife was. Godparents: the baby's own eldest sister Maria and the man she married in this parish four months later.

The mothers are the finding - *** Beloqui, Echeverry and Pelaez are Basque. *** Also disproved this archive's own claim that a daughter of the Montevideo trunk was baptised here.

column1: Uruguay, Civil Registration - Montevideo death certificate No. 216 of 24 December 1901
column2: *** THE DEATH OF LUIS EUGENIO LERENA LENGUAS, closing a question this archive held open all day. *** Image read. Died at calle Suarez 25, el Paso del Molino, aged 56, "de profesion HACENDADO", of pulmonary tuberculosis; his mother Justiniana Lenguas alive at 79 in the same house. Found only by searching the MOTHER's name - FamilySearch indexes him as Luis SERENA Lenguas.

column1: Uruguay Catholic Church Records - searched on JUSTINIANA LENGUAS as mother
column2: *** Four siblings of Luis Eugenio, and GILBERTO LERENA among them. *** Two independent records of Gilberto's own children give his parents as Luis and Justiniana Lenguas, which makes the co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book a brother of the man whose daughter was baptised at Rosario in 1866. Index-level; the images are not yet opened.

column1: Uruguay collections searched on CANDIDO JUANICO as father
column2: *** Confirms the two-wives inference this archive made from dates alone. *** Julia, b.1842, by Juliana Joaquina Gonzalez; and Sara, Zara Sista Emirena and Celia JUANICO LENGUAS, b.1866-69, by SIXTA LENGUAS. A full generation apart. Note the second wife's surname against Justiniana Lenguas - the two families look connected before 1864.

column1: Argentina, National Census 1869 - the Rosario LORENA household schedule, image ark 3:1:S3HT-XK5Q-L
column2: *** SIX LORENAS READ AT THEIR OWN SCHEDULE, and set down. *** All six are one household. The head, Agustin Lorena, 40, is a tinsmith of LIMA - the provincia column blank because he is not Argentine - with five Cordoba-born children. The clerk wrote LORENA with an O and a single L. Two of the children were flagged as the right age to be a parent in 1882; they are a Peruvian tinsmith's family and not this one.

Avena, Martini, Rodriguez, Acosta, Coppes, Coman, Fernandez, Duarte, Pero, Amaral, Nunez, Cassavola, Ledda, Blasi, Lopez, Lentini, Toledo, Ruiz, Rosas, Flores, Rabellino, Ramosfe, Gallego. column1: FamilySearch catalogue 208788 - Registros parroquiales de Nuestra Senora del Rosario, 1722-1961, all 73 film rows
column2: *** THE DEATH REGISTERS FOR THE WHOLE INDEX GAP ARE FILMED, and this archive had listed only one of the five. *** Defunciones 1731-1803 (DGS 4531019), 1804-1824+1828-1841 (4531020), 1841-1860 (4531021), 1861-1864 (4531022), 1864-1875 (4531023). The catalogue also confirms the hard edge: THERE IS NO DEFUNCIONES FILM AFTER 1875. Also recovered: three Confirmaciones films and two earlier Matrimonios films, none previously listed here.

column1: San Francisco de Asis, Montevideo - baptism act No. 1447, folio 504 (31 October 1886)
column2: *** THE ACT THAT MAKES GILBERTO A BROTHER, ON A DOCUMENT. *** His daughter Maria Angelica Julia, "hija legitima de Don Gilberto Lerena y de Dona Julia Salvanach, orientales", with paternal grandparents "Don LUIS y Dona JUSTINIANA LENGUAS" - the same couple named as Luis Eugenio's parents. AND THE GODMOTHER IS DONA JULIA JUANICO DE LERENA, Luis Eugenio's own wife. Same priest, Martin Perez, as act 1720.

column1: Uruguay, Civil Registration - Montevideo birth certificate No. 283 of 1908
column2: Jose Julio's birth, declared by HIS OWN MOTHER at 64, a widow. It independently confirms Luis Eugenio's death on 24 December 1901 from a different document - and places *** JUSTINIANA LENGUAS, AT EIGHTY-SEVEN, RESIDENT IN THE ARGENTINE REPUBLIC. ***

column1: San Francisco de Asis, Montevideo - baptism acts Nos. 404 and 405, folio 274 (4 October 1843)
column2: Julia Juanico's own baptism, image read: born 23 November 1842, "hija legitima de D. Candido Juanico y D. Juliana Joaquina Gonzalez". And act 404 immediately above it baptises *** ENRIQUE JUANICO, born 18 May 1841, a BROTHER *** - christened the same day. A name trap: Julia's godfather is also a D. Enrique Juanico, and a boy of two cannot stand godfather.

column1: La Mauricia, Villa de la Union, Montevideo - baptisms of 7 January 1846
column2: *** LUIS EUGENIO'S OWN BAPTISM, and the generation above it. *** Born 9 February 1843; "hijo legitimo de Luis Lerena y Justiniana Lenguas, orientales. Paternos: Francisco y Maria Fernandez. Maternos: Pedro y Carmen Gonzalez." His sister's act calls the maternal grandfather "el GENERAL D. Pedro Lenguas". A sixth sibling found: ALEJANDRO. These are later transcripts from a legajo, which matters - see the 1850 act.

column1: S. Agustin, pueblo de la Restauracion, Montevideo - baptism act No. 585, 7 October 1850
column2: *** THE ACT THAT PUTS SANCHO ON A DOCUMENT. *** Alberto Octavio Lerena, born 22 March 1850, "hijo legitimo de D. Luis Lerena y Dona Justiniana Lenguas, naturales de Montevideo. PATERNOS: D. SANCHO y Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ." Opened specifically to resolve a conflict with the 1846 transcripts, which name the paternal grandfather FRANCISCO. The original beats the copy.

column1: Uruguay, Civil Registration - Montevideo death registration of Sixta Lenguas, 17 January 1884
column2: *** THE RECORD THAT MAKES JUSTINIANA AND SIXTA SISTERS. *** Parents "Pedro Lenguas, Carmen Gonzalez", husband "Candido Juanico" - the same parents the 1846 acts give Justiniana. So the groom's maternal aunt was already the bride's stepmother when Luis Eugenio married Julia Juanico in 1864.

column2: Six more acts read act by act: Pedro Toledo, Miguel Dolmas, Rosa Perez, Maria Candelaria, Alejandro Orellana, Arturo Ferrari. No Lerena. *** 786 consecutive baptisms now read. ***

column1: Rosario cathedral, Defunciones 1841-1860 - film 1091422, DGS 4531021
column2: *** THE DEATH REGISTERS STARTED. *** 658 images, unrestricted; the leader card reads 1091422, matching the catalogue. First opening read: five acts, 26 May to 18 June 1841 - Juan Fernandez, Luisa Candelaria Bravo, Victoria Medina, Ynnocencia Villa Real, Maria Zumbero. No Lerena. The margin-name method works here exactly as on the baptisms. On the order of six thousand acts for 1841-1860 alone: STARTED, not finished.

column1: FamilySearch catalogue 208788 re-read while their SEARCH was down - the confirmation and early marriage films
column2: DGS numbers recovered for five films this archive had listed without them: *** Confirmaciones 1883-1918 (DGS 4531018) - the one that covers Pablo Armando *** - plus Confirmaciones 1722-1833/1860-1895 (4531017), Confirmaciones 1764-1833 (4530427), Matrimonios 1722-1803 (4531037) and Matrimonios 1804-1852 (4531038). A DIAGNOSTIC WORTH KEEPING: catalogue SEARCH, full-text and /search/film/<old film number> were all erroring, while a DIRECT CATALOGUE ID still worked.

column1: Catedral Basilica de Montevideo - baptism of Raul Alfredo Luis Lerena, folio 296, 10 September 1885
column2: *** THE SECOND WITNESS TO GILBERTO'S PARENTAGE, and from a different parish. *** "Hijo legitimo de Gilberto Lerena y Julia Salvanach, orientales: abuelos paternos LUIS y JUSTINIANA LENGUAS" - identical to act 1447 of 1886 but in another year, another church and another hand. Godmother a JOSEFA LERENA otherwise unknown here.

column1: Arzobispado de Buenos Aires - informacion matrimonial, Nuestra Senora del Socorro (Retiro), folio 44, 25 March 1914
column2: *** CORRECTS THIS ARCHIVE TWICE. *** The record is an informacion matrimonial, not the "Retiro baptism" the register called it; and the father read as "ALBERTO (almost certainly GILBERTO)" is written GILBERTO plainly. Carlos Lerena, 30, of Pueyrredon 1750, "bautizado en la Iglesia de el CORDON, Dep. de Montevideo" - naming a third Montevideo parish for this family - marrying Rosa Maria Eppens.

column1: Uruguay, Civil Registration - Montevideo death act No. 45 of 17 January 1884, Sixta Lenguas
column2: *** PUTS THE SISTERS FINDING ON AN IMAGE, AND ADDS TWO GENERATIONS. *** "Hija de D. Pedro Lenguas y de Dona Carmen Gonzalez, finados; sus abuelos paternos D. ANTONIO LENGUAS y Dona JUANA GRANDAL; maternos D. PASCUAL GONZALEZ y Dona JOSEFA GRANDAL." Her husband recorded as "D. Candido Juanico, Oriental, edad 72 anos, viudo, ABOGADO".

column1: Rosario cathedral, Confirmaciones 1883-1918 - film 1091419, DGS 4531018
column2: *** OPENED FOR THE FIRST TIME. *** Listed as untried since this archive's first week and without a film number until 13 September. The confirmations of 26 March 1890 at Rosario are a numbered list naming each child's PARENTS - and Pablo Armando, born February 1882, is squarely inside the age range of six to fifteen. First page read: eleven entries, no Lerena, and *** every one of them a girl ***, which suggests the confirmations were taken sex by sex and that a boy of eight is in a separate run of pages.

column1: Rosario cathedral, Defunciones 1841-1860 - two more openings
column2: Acts of 22 July to 14 August 1841 read: Pedro Pablo, Jose Santiago, Matias Lopez, Fermin Sosa, Ambrosia Garcia, Felicia Dias, Ana Maria Leguisamon, Gregorio Paez, Eleuterio Morales. No Lerena. *** TWO THINGS THAT CHANGE THE ESTIMATE: the film carries a "POOR COPY - WHOLE VOLUME" target card, which is FamilySearch's own warning on the filming of the entire volume; and it contains RE-SHOTS, so 658 images is not 658 openings. ***

column1: Rosario cathedral, Libro 25 - opening at i=20, acts 951-956 (10-11 August 1882)
column2: Bernal, Parodi, Cavarozzi, Lopez, Rodriguez, Echague. No Lerena. *** 792 consecutive baptisms now read act by act. ***

column1: Argentina, Capital Federal Catholic Church Records and Argentine military records - searched on GILBERTO LERENA AS FATHER
column2: *** THE ARGENTINE LIMB OF THE MONTEVIDEO HOUSE, assembled for the first time: EIGHT children of Gilberto Lerena and Julia Salvanach. *** Four born at Montevideo (1878-1886), four at Buenos Aires (1890-1898) - which BRACKETS the family's crossing between 31 October 1886 and 29 October 1890, firmer than the "1887 to 1889" read off census birthplaces. *** And Juan Carlos is not among them. ***

column1: Uruguayan and Argentine collections - searched for ALEJANDRO LERENA
column2: Run to test whether Alejandro Lerena Lenguas, b. 29 May 1845, is the ALEJANDRO MAXIMO LERENA of the enrolment cards. *** INCONCLUSIVE, and recorded as such: no record found names Alejandro Maximo's parents. *** The search did establish that there are at least THREE distinct men of the name, including one of the Trinidad orbit married to Severa Fernandez - which is the mistake this file exists to prevent.

column1: Rosario cathedral, Confirmaciones 1883-1918 - four more images
column2: Entries 45-88, 133-177 and 222-243 of the 26 March 1890 sitting, and the opening of a SECOND 1890 sitting in June-July. No Lerena. *** The first page's apparent all-girls pattern turned out to be an artefact of eleven rows: boys are mixed straight in. *** Ages run from two to fourteen in one sitting, so nobody can be ruled in or out by age.

column1: Argentina, Capital Federal Catholic Church Records - the marriage of Luis Lerena and Justiniana Lenguas, 3 March 1842
column2: *** THE GENERATION ABOVE THE TRUNK, MARRYING - reached by searching the surname LENGUAS in ARGENTINA, which nobody had tried. *** Luis Lerena, 30, of Montevideo, "hijo legitimo de D. SANCHO y Dona Maria Fernandez" - Sancho for the third time and the earliest - *** and "desposé en SEGUNDAS NUPCIAS ... VIUDO de Dona CAROLINA", so he had a first wife nobody here knew of. *** Justiniana, 20, "hija legitima del Sr. GRAL. Lenguas y Dona Carmen Gonzalez". FamilySearch indexes the rank as a forename, "Geraldo Dios Lenguas".

column1: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo - marriage petition of Luis Lerena and Carolina Oliva, 3 September 1836
column2: *** THE FIRST MARRIAGE, found within an hour of learning there had been one. *** On the stamped paper of 1836 and signed by Luis Lerena in his own hand: "hijo legitimo de D. SANCHO LERENA y de Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ ... tiene concertado matrimonio con Dona CAROLINA OLIVA". *** Sancho's earliest and plainest attestation - a fourth record - closing the doubt raised by two 1846 transcripts. *** FamilySearch files it under a Colombian collection by mistake.

column1: Uruguayan collections searched for CHILDREN of Luis Lerena and Carolina Oliva, 1836-1842
column2: *** A NULL, and an honest one. *** No record anywhere pairs a Lerena father with a Carolina Oliva mother; and every Carolina Oliva in the Uruguayan records of that span belongs to a later woman who married Antonio Reverditto. The 1836 marriage left no indexed trace but its own petition. Not an exclusion - the Montevideo registers of 1837-1841 are largely un-indexed, and this archive has twice this week found what indexes miss.

column1: Nuestra Senora del Carmen la Mayor, Cordon, Montevideo - baptism of 13 December 1831
column2: *** THE PRESIDENT OF URUGUAY STOOD GODFATHER TO SANCHO LLERENA'S GRANDSON. *** "Fueron padrinos Don FRUCTUOSO RIVERA, PRESIDENTE DE LA REPUBLICA, y su esposa Dona Bernardina Fragoso." The act also produces JUSTA PASTORA LERENA, "natural de Canelones" - a DAUGHTER of Sancho and a SISTER of Don Luis, unknown to this archive - and names Sancho and Maria Fernandez as maternal grandparents. Found through FULL-TEXT, which reads the handwriting; no search on LERENA would have returned it.

column1: Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Canelones - Religious Marriage Investigation Files 1776-1806
column2: *** SANCHO LLERENA IN PERSON, under oath. *** "Presento por testigo en esta Vicaria a SANCHO LLERENA, a quien se le recivio juramento que lo hizo... bajo del cual prometio decir verdad." He appears as a sworn witness in another man's marriage investigation at Canelones - a primary document naming him, where this archive had only a user-built tree.

column1: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo - baptism of October 1833
column2: *** THE ACT THAT REOPENED THE SANCHO QUESTION AN HOUR AFTER THIS ARCHIVE CLOSED IT. *** A second child of Justa Pastora Lerena, naming her parents "Maternos: FRANCISCO LERINA y Maria Fernandez" - and it is an ORIGINAL, not one of the 1846 transcripts the copies-versus-originals argument rested on. Its godparents are ABELINO and DOMINGA LERENA, two more of that generation.

column1: Full-text search for the phrase "Llerena y Aguilar"
column2: *** THIRTY HITS, EVERY ONE IN QUITO, ECUADOR *** - an Antonio Llerena y Aguilar of the Quito notarial records, 1789-1824. So the "Aguilar" this archive carries in Sancho's name is supported by no record it has read, and comes from the FamilySearch Tree.

column1: Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Canelones - Baptism Records 1794-1810 and Confirmation Records 1804
column2: *** SANCHO LLERENA AT HOME, IN 1804 - twenty-seven years earlier than anything this archive held two days ago. *** His daughter DOMINGA JOSEFA baptised 15 May 1804, "hija legitima de Sancho Llerena y de Maria Fernandez" - and she is the Dominga Lerena who stood godmother at the Catedral de Montevideo in 1833, so a SISTER of Don Luis. In the same year's confirmation list he stands godfather to "Jose, esclavo de Manuel Lopez". Found through FULL-TEXT; neither act is name-indexed.

column1: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo - baptism of 4 July 1837
column2: *** A SECOND BROTHER FOR DON LUIS, AND THE FIRST WIFE'S REAL SURNAME. *** "Hija legitima de D. PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA natural de esta y de Dna Vicenta Vega natural de Cerro Largo. Abuelos Paternos: D. SANCHO y Dna Maria Fernandez. Padrinos: D. LUIS LERENA y Dna CAROLINA ORIBE." *** So the bride of 1836 is ORIBE, not the OLIVA this archive recorded twice from FamilySearch's index - and the published genealogy, tiered SECONDARY here, was right that he married a daughter of an Oribe. *** She was also alive in July 1837.

column1: Full-text re-run of the central null, WITHOUT the filter that breaks the search
column2: *** THE NULL HOLDS. *** "Juan Carlos Lerena" as an exact phrase across the whole corpus returns TWO documents: the Montevideo dispensation of Juan Carlos Gonzalez Lerena, b.1899, already recorded here as not ours; and a Montevideo death of 2001 for a Juan Carlos ATAY Lerena, b.1933. Re-run because the recordCountry filter was found to break full-text silently, casting doubt on earlier nulls. This one was sound.

column1: Full-text search for children of Luis Lerena and Carolina Oribe, 1836-1842
column2: *** A MUCH STRONGER NULL THAN THE INDEXED ONE, because the coverage was checked first. *** The Montevideo registers for those years ARE in the full-text corpus - Cordon baptisms 1837-1841, Catedral baptisms 1836-1840, Catedral deaths 1836-1842 - so the handwriting has been read. Neither "de Don Luis Lerena" nor "Lerena y de Carolina" returns a baptism from them. The marriage appears to have left no surviving child's act in either parish.

column1: Montevideo civil marriage registers 1902-1914 - full-text on the compound surname LERENA JUANICO
column2: *** THE SIXTH CHILD WAS A JUDGE. *** Thirty-five acts open "Por ante mi JULIO LERENA JUANICO, JUEZ DE PAZ y OFICIAL DEL ESTADO CIVIL de la Primera Seccion del Departamento de Montevideo"; one read in full (Maronas, 28 Aug 1909). Almost certainly JOSE JULIO, b. 15 March 1879 - the only Julio among the seven children - which also explains why his mother registered his birth when he was twenty-nine. Found only by searching the COMPOUND surname, never tried here before.

column1: Rosario cathedral, Libro 25 - opening at i=21, acts 957-962 (12-13 August 1882)
column2: Panelo, Gonzalez, Sanchez, Vidal, Aranda, Mujica. No Lerena. *** 798 consecutive baptisms now read act by act. ***

column1: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records JUNE 1913
column2: *** A NINTH LERENA DISPENSATION, missed by this archive's own sweep of the same register. *** Jose Pedro Massera's petition of 19 June 1913 to be dispensed one conciliar proclama in order to marry "Dona EMA SIXTA LERENA JUANICO, feligresa de la metropolitana", eleven days before the wedding. Missed because the sweep searched "LERENA FELIGRESA" and her compound surname sits between those words.

column1: Direccion de Cementerios, Montevideo - mortality return for December 1901
column2: *** A THIRD INDEPENDENT RECORD OF LUIS EUGENIO'S DEATH, and it places his burial. *** "Relacion de los individuos que han fallecido en el mes de Diciembre de 1901" lists LUIS LERENA LENGUAS against day 24, between Lucrecia Sosa and Emilia Zanola de Sanchez. Agrees exactly with civil act No. 216 and with his widow's sworn statement of 1908. Found only by searching the COMPOUND surname - a search on LERENA does not reach a table of names.

column1: Argentina, National Census 1895 - the household schedule of Gilberto Lerena, Seccion 21, Manzana 15
column2: *** CITED SINCE WEEK ONE FOR NAMES; NEVER READ AS A HOUSEHOLD UNTIL NOW. *** Sixteen people on one page. It gives Gilberto a trade - CORREDOR DE COMERCIO; enters JUSTINIANA LENGUAS at 73 and VIUDA, so Don Luis Lerena was dead by 1895; resolves a contradiction this archive had flagged against itself (Maria E. C. is 26 and SOLTERA, not Gilberto's daughter); and finds *** JOSEFA "LERENA DE LERENA", a widow of 43 *** - almost certainly the Josefa Lerena who stood godmother at Montevideo in 1885.

column1: Uruguay, Civil Registration - Montevideo death registration No. 10 of 3 April 1947
column2: *** THE LERENA TRAIBEL BRANCH PLACED AT LAST. *** JOSEFA LORENA LERENA TRAIBEL, died 2 April 1947 aged NINETY-SIX, born 1851, "Parents: AMBROCIA TRAIBEL, AVELINO LERENA". This archive has named that branch since its first week without ever placing Avelino. She is a strong candidate for the Josefa Lerena of the 1885 Montevideo font and the "Lerena de L. Josefa, 43, viuda" of Gilberto's 1895 Buenos Aires household - *** recorded as three separate rows and deliberately NOT merged, *** after this archive conflated two Arturo Lerenas in the same week.

column1: Uruguay, Civil Registration - the Moratorio Lerena children, and the tree attachment behind them
column2: *** THE RECORD THAT DEFLATED MY OWN CLAIM WITHIN THE HOUR. *** A JOSEFA LERENA appears as mother of Josefa, Eduardo and Maria MORATORIO LERENA, "Spouses: Fernando Moratorio" - index-level civil registration, real records. FamilySearch's TREE then attaches her to Josefa Lerena Traibel 1851-1947, which is SECONDARY. If that link holds, the 1895 census "Lerena de L." is the enumerator's shorthand for the household and NOT evidence of a Lerena-Lerena marriage.

column1: ALEX - Historische Rechts- und Gesetzestexte, Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek (alex.onb.ac.at)
column2: *** ASSESSED AND UNUSABLE TODAY, for a reason worth recording. *** Its full-text search returns "TOTAL (0)" plus "Diese Seite steht zur Zeit leider noch nicht zur Verfugung" for EVERY query - proved by controls: "Konsul", "Uruguay" and "Montevideo" each give the identical 166-byte response. A zero from a search that returns zero for everything is not evidence. The one genuine hook if it recovers is CONSULAR: Austria-Hungary had consulates at Montevideo and Buenos Aires and gazetted its consuls, and this family is exactly the class honorary consuls were drawn from.

column1: Full-text search for the phrase "Sancho Lerena" - the Madrid notarial cluster
column2: A real DON SANCHO LERENA appears in Madrid notarial records 1773-1808, among censos and chaplaincies. *** NOT OURS, on a date: ours was marrying at Canelones in January 1791 while this man transacts before a Madrid notary the same year. *** Recorded because it is exactly the find that gets mistaken for him later - right name, right decade, and a Spanish origin that would flatter this archive's own Andalusian hypothesis.

column1: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion - two baptisms at Union, Montevideo, 8 March 1880
column2: *** THE ACT THAT SETTLES JOSEFA, and converts a tree attachment into a parish record. *** Maria Carlota and Maria de las Mercedes Moratorio Lerena, "de Fernando Moratorio y Josefa Lerena", with maternal grandparents "AVELINO y AMBROSIA TRAIBEL". So Josefa Lerena Traibel married a MORATORIO - which kills this archive's own census reading of "Lerena de Lerena" on a document rather than on a tree. It also produces MERCEDES LERENA, godmother and very likely Josefa's sister.

column1: Catedral Basilica de Montevideo - marriage of 3 February 1892
column2: *** A TENTH LERENA DISPENSATION, and a second child for Avelino. *** ALFREDO GERENA [LERENA], 35, "hijo legitimo de Don Avelino Lorena y Dona Ambrosia Traibel", married Hermenegilda Carolina Gavarro - the couple DISPENSED OF CONSANGUINITY in the third degree with atingencia to the second by Archbishop MARIANO SOLER personally. His mother stood witness. *** Missed by this archive's dispensation sweep two ways at once: the groom is spelled GERENA, a seventh variant, and the dispensation clause precedes the names. ***

column1: San Francisco de Asis, Montevideo - two baptisms of 12 March 1858
column2: *** THE ACT THAT ATTACHES THE LERENA TRAIBEL BRANCH TO THE TRUNK. *** Alfredo Justiniano and Ana Rosario, children of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel, with paternal grandparents SANCHO LERENA and MARIA FERNANDEZ named twice on one page. *** AND THE GODPARENTS ARE LAVALLEJA - Justiniano, Constantino and Ana. *** With Fructuoso Rivera at a font in 1831 and an Oribe for a bride in 1836, this family now stands at fonts with all three caudillo houses of Uruguayan independence. No relationship to any of them is claimed.

column1: FamilySearch records search - the CHILDREN OF SANCHO LERENA AND MARIA FERNANDEZ, searched as a couple
column2: *** THE APEX GENERATION, COMPLETED BY SEARCHING THE PARENTS RATHER THAN THE SURNAME. *** Twenty-two results for father Sancho + mother Maria Fernandez in Uruguay, of which four are new: *** AVELINO'S DATES (born 1815, died 22 August 1890, Montevideo civil registration 23 Aug, ark 1:1:62J2-4CNQ) ***; *** JUSTA PASTORA'S MARRIAGE (3 November 1830, Cordon, to MANUEL BARROS, ark 1:1:X9PT-MQTQ) ***; and TWO records for a DOMINGA with DIFFERENT HUSBANDS - Antonio Rodriguez (ark 1:1:6D7C-5X1Y) and Antonio Ruiz de Carvallo (ark 1:1:6DF7-HZPR), NOT merged and both images unopened. *** Avelino's death date explains why his widow rather than he stood witness at their son's 1892 wedding: he had been dead sixteen months. *** The method is the finding: this family is indexed under eight spellings, so the surname box loses records the PARENT PAIR recovers.
column4: SECONDARY - indexes read, images not yet opened

column1: FamilySearch records search - JUAN CARLOS LERENA, by the parent-pair method, Argentina and Uruguay
column2: *** THE CENTRAL NULL SURVIVES THE BEST METHOD THIS ARCHIVE HAS. *** Argentina, father "Juan Carlos" + Lerena: 210 results, and the only Juan Carlos Lerena among them is PABLO ARMANDO'S OWN ENROLMENT CARD. Uruguay, as a person: 822 results, of which ONE is a Juan Carlos Lerena recorded as a father - *** opened and ruled out, an infant death registered 21 February 1983. *** Also observed: nearly every Juan Carlos Lerena in Uruguay carries LERENA AS A SECOND, MATERNAL SURNAME - Gonzalez Lerena, Carvalho Lerena, del Campo Lerena, Reyes Lerena. *** AND A FAILURE MODE FOUND: FamilySearch renders "Historical Record Search Results (0)" WHILE THE QUERY IS STILL RUNNING. *** Three false nulls were caught only by a control query on Sancho, which also returned zero and was known to be wrong. See data/parent-pair-search-method.tsv.

column1: Capilla de la Mauricia, Villa de la Union, Montevideo - the whole page of 7 January 1846
column2: *** RE-READ END TO END rather than entry by entry, and it corrected a branch. *** ALEJANDRO is a son of AVELINO LERENA and AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, born 29 May 1843, with LUIS and JUSTINIANA as his GODPARENTS - this archive had recorded him as their sixth child, born 1845. *** And every act on the page, Lerena and not, ends "asi consta del LEGAJO conservado en este Archivo, mandado TRASLADAR por el Senor Obispo D. JACINTO VERA" - the page is a bundle of loose papers copied into a book three years late. *** THE CAUSE IS THE GUERRA GRANDE: the siege closed in February 1843, the three children were born February, May and July 1843, and none was christened until 1846 - in the VILLA DE LA UNION, which Oribe renamed the VILLA RESTAURACION and made his seat. *** Also carries a contradiction in the source: two full siblings born 9 February and 30 July of the same year. ***
column4: PRIMARY - full-text transcript of the whole page read

column1: Registro Civil de Montevideo - certified copy of the 1846 act, issued 23 September 1920
column2: *** A SECOND, INDEPENDENT WITNESS TO LUIS EUGENIO'S BAPTISM, seventy-four years later. *** Film 008166522 item 2, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2C-J9J2-K, filed among Montevideo baptism records of August-November 1920 - which is why FamilySearch indexes this man as born 1919 and christened 1920. The certificate transcribes the 1846 act in full and agrees with the parish page word for word, including "nacio el nueve de Febrero del ano cuarenta y tres" and "Paternos FRANCISCO y MARIA FERNANDEZ". *** Useful twice: it confirms the reading, and it shows that acts of the 1840s surface inside twentieth-century films where no date filter will ever find them. ***

column1: ALEX - Historische Rechts- und Gesetzestexte, Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek (alex.onb.ac.at)
column2: *** ASSESSED ON REQUEST, AND THE ASSESSMENT IS THAT IT CANNOT BE ASSESSED TODAY. *** About five million pages of Austrian and Habsburg official text. Its full-text search returns the same stub for every query - *** established by CONTROLS, not assumed: "Konsul", "Uruguay" and "Montevideo" each returned an identical 166-byte response. *** A word certain to appear in five million pages of Austrian law returning zero is a broken search, not a null. RETESTED 14 Sep by submitting the site's own form as a POST rather than the GET used first - a stricter test, since a malformed request could have explained the first result. The form comes back unchanged. *** On relevance, honestly: THE PRIOR IS LOW *** - this family is Uruguayan, Argentine, Spanish, South African and British, and nothing in the record touches the Habsburg lands. *** The one real hook is CONSULAR: *** Austria-Hungary kept consulates at Montevideo and Buenos Aires and the Hof- und Staatshandbuch lists consuls, so an Austro-Hungarian honorary consulship held by a Lerena in the River Plate would show. It would NOT show Pablo Armando's own claimed consulship, which was Argentine and at the Cape.

column1: FamilySearch full text - the compound "LERENA LERENA", the sharpest test of the central question
column2: *** IF MARIA LERENA WAS A LERENA BY BIRTH, HER CHILDREN WOULD CARRY THE COMPOUND. Nobody had ever searched for it. *** Run first against the Uruguayan Catholic registers (4 hits) and then against the whole corpus without a country filter (43 hits). *** EVERY SINGLE ONE IS A TRANSCRIPTION DOUBLING at a line or page end *** - "Pio Lerena . Lerena", "Zelmira Lerena , Lerena argentino", "Celidonio B. de Lerena Lerena", "G. Lerena Lerena" across a printed title page. Each was opened and each transcript read. The only genuine compounds in all 43 are COLOMBIAN, a different family in Bolivar. *** So no child of two Lerenas is recorded under the compound anywhere FamilySearch has transcribed. This LOWERS the probability that Maria Lerena was a Lerena by birth; it does not close it *** - a woman can be a Lerena by birth without her children ever being written so, and Rosario's parish books are thin in full text.
column4: SECONDARY - a controlled negative across 43 opened documents

column1: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo - Marriage Dispensation Records, July-August 1911
column2: *** THE ELEVENTH LERENA DISPENSATION, and the only one that draws its own family tree. *** Under "Esquemas explicativos de los grados de parentesco" the Cura Vicario sets out two lines: BERNABE LERENA married FLORENCIA CARDOZO, and his sister MARIA LERENA married her brother ELISEO CARDOZO - so their children CUSTODIO LERENA and EMA CARDOZO are DOUBLE FIRST COUSINS, which is why the tie had to be traced twice. *** They asked to be excused the fee, "pues no pueden satisfacerlos" - a poor Lerena household, in an archive that has spent two days finding generals, judges and hacendados. *** AND IT CARRIES A DOCUMENTED MARIA LERENA of roughly the right generation - recorded so she is ruled out ON THE RECORD, since she married a Cardozo where Pablo Armando's mother stands beside Juan Carlos Lerena. *** THE STANDING CONCLUSION SURVIVES: eleven dispensations, and every Lerena in every one of them marries out. ***

column1: Iglesia Matriz de Montevideo - baptism of 30 June 1789
column2: *** THE EARLIEST RECORD OF SANCHO LLERENA ANYWHERE IN THIS ARCHIVE - fifteen years further back than anything held yesterday, and two years before his own marriage. *** "Padrinos SANCHO LLERENA y Juliana Josefa Cornejo" at the baptism of Juana, daughter of "NICOLAS BENTENO, INDIO NATURAL DE LA CIUDAD DEL TUCUMAN, y de Leonarda Correa de Buenos Ayres". He is about twenty-two and in MONTEVIDEO, not Canelones. *** And it is the second time this archive has found him sponsoring at the margins of colonial society: in 1804 he stood godfather to an ENSLAVED MAN, here to the daughter of an indigenous man from Tucuman. Twice, fifteen years apart. *** The act calls him SANCHO.

column1: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo - baptism of 12 May 1827
column2: *** SANCHO'S DAUGHTER DOMINGA MARRIED A CAPTAIN, and the act says so. *** "Lucinda Gregoria del Corazon de Jesus ... hija legitima del CAPITAN DON ANTONIO RUIZ DE CARVALLO y de DONA DOMINGA LLERENA DE CARVALLO. Nieta Paterna del MAYOR DON JOAQUIN RUIZ DE CARVALLO ... Materna de SANCHO LLERENA y de Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ." *** The godfather is the EXCELENTISIMO SENOR GENERAL DON FRANCISCO DE PAULA MAGGESI. *** AND IT IDENTIFIES A WOMAN THIS ARCHIVE COULD NOT PLACE: the "Dona Dominga Carvallo" who stood godmother at a Lerena font in 1850 is almost certainly this woman - a Lerena by birth, standing for her brother's son.

column1: Nuestra Senora del Carmen la Mayor, Cordon - the MARRIAGE ACT of 3 November 1830
column2: *** THE ACT ITSELF, not the index - and it puts a tree's claim on a document. *** "precedidas informacion de libertad de MANUEL ZEFERINO BARROS natural de PERNAMBUCO, hijo legitimo de Jose [P]olanda de Barros y de Ana Maria Cabalgante, sobre el Matrimonio que libremente quiere contraer con JUSTA PASTORA LLERENA, NATURAL DE CANELONES, RESIDENTE EN EL CORDON, hija legitima de SANCHO LLERENA y de *** MARIA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS ***." This archive has carried TRESGUERRAS from a published tree since its first week, marked secondary and unverified. *** The tree was right, about something no index gives - which raises the standing of its other unopened claim, that Sancho and Maria married at Canelones on 8 January 1791. *** The parish is Damaso Antonio Larranaga's; he is marrying another couple on the same page.

column1: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo - baptism of 25 October 1840
column2: *** THE ACT THAT CLOSED THE TWO-DOMINGA PROBLEM, on the day it was raised. *** "Bautice solemnemente a DOMINGO que nacio el cuatro de Agosto, hijo legitimo de D. ANTONIO RODRIGUEZ DE CARBALLO, natural de la PROVINCIA DEL RIO GRANDE, y de Dona DOMINGA LERENA, natural del Estado Oriental. Nieto paterno de D. JOAQUIN RODRIGUEZ y de Dona JUANA DEL ESPIRITU SANTO, ambos naturales de la COLONIA DEL SACRAMENTO, y por parte materna de D. SANCHO LERENA y de Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ." *** Set beside the 1827 act it shows that "Antonio Rodriguez" and "Antonio Ruiz de Carvallo" are ONE MAN whose first surname the registers write two ways - so there is ONE Dominga, not two. *** The archive had held the two records apart, unmerged, precisely until an act joined them.

column1: England, Devon, Parish Registers (Devon Record Office), 1529-1974
column2: *** THE TAYLOR MARRIAGES, TAKEN OFF A TREE AND PUT ON PARISH REGISTERS. *** Five of Mary Septima's siblings were recorded here as bare surnames with no forename, date, place or source. All five are now named: *** HENRY DALLING m. Isabella Temple Taylor at NORTHAM, 10 Sep 1900; HENRY ALBERT BURTON m. Irene Taylor at NORTHAM, 30 Aug 1900; CHARLES WILLIAM BELL m. Margaret Helen Walker Taylor, banns NORTHAM 22 Nov 1903; WILLIAM NORRISH SWEET m. Lucy Elizabeth Taylor, banns CHURSTON FERRERS 1909; ALFRED SIDNEY WOOD m. Agnes Walker Taylor, Devon 1918; and HORACE ARCHIBALD TAYLOR m. MARY JANE MARSHALL, banns NORTHAM 17 Dec 1893. *** TWO SISTERS MARRIED AT NORTHAM ELEVEN DAYS APART in 1900, four months after their mother's death. *** *** The method matters: TAYLOR returns 705,979 results in England, so the RARE surname must be the principal and Taylor the spouse - and where both are common, the sisters' distinctive forenames do the work.
column4: PRIMARY - parish register index read; the register images not yet opened

column1: England and Wales, Census, 1911
column2: *** THE CENSUS THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER READ - it held only 1891 and 1901, both of the parental household. *** By 1911 William Taylor was nine years dead and the family had scattered. It yields FIVE OF MARY SEPTIMA'S NIECES AND NEPHEWS at one stroke - Horace Henry Charles, Ronald William James and Sylvia Mary DALLING at Northam; Charles William and Albert Edward BURTON at Bideford - Henry Dalling's trade (GARDENER, DOMESTIC) and his age, and *** the fact that KATHLEEN GEORGINA TAYLOR was SINGLE at forty-one and living in her married sister's house. *** That last replaces a tree's silence with a document.

column1: England and Wales, Censuses of 1871, 1901 and 1911 - the Taylors of Bideford and Northam
column2: *** THE 1871 CENSUS SETTLES A QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE HAD WRITTEN DOWN AND LEFT: *** it has KATHLEEN GEORGINA and WILLIAM JOHN both as infants in the house on 2 April 1871, and their parents' banns were called at Bideford on 9 January 1870 - so they are TWINS, born November 1870, and the family had TWO sets of twins. *** THE 1901 AND 1911 CENSUSES NAME WILLIAM JOHN'S WIFE AS "FANNY HELEN" and date the marriage to 1892 *** - where a tree said "Fanny Ellen JEFFEREY", a surname no record supports. *** AND THEY SHOW TWO OF THE TEN SIBLINGS IN THE SAME CORNER OF SOUTH DEVON: *** William John at PAIGNTON by 1911, Lucy Elizabeth's banns at CHURSTON FERRERS three miles away in 1909, both eighty miles from Northam where they were born. The brother was there first.

column1: FamilySearch full text - the Rosario films, tested for transcripts rather than assumed
column2: *** A METHOD UNLOCK AND A MEASURED LIMIT. *** This archive had assumed since its first week that the Rosario registers must be read by assembling DeepZoom tiles. *** THE CONFIRMATIONS FILM - DGS 4531018, the one that covers Pablo Armando - IS FULLY TRANSCRIBED IN FULL TEXT: *** about 4,000 characters an image, every entry giving "NAME de N anos hijo legitimo de FATHER y MOTHER" plus a godparent. It can be read one request at a time. The DEATHS film, DGS 4531019, is NOT transcribed and covers only 1731-1864, so it cannot hold anyone this archive is chasing. *** AND A HARD LIMIT: unquoted terms are OR'd, not AND'd *** - "Lerena Rosario difunto" returns 17,782,105 documents - so full text accepts exactly ONE quoted phrase and narrowing must be done by choosing a rarer phrase, never by adding words. *** The place facet is a trap: f.recordPlace on a full-text query returns a confident ZERO with "No filters available" against every heading. *** The third false-null caught on this service in one day.

column1: Uruguayan civil registration - ZELMIRA CARLOTA LERENA LARRIERA
column2: *** A CANDIDATE TESTED AND RULED OUT, which is the point of recording candidates. *** Flagged this morning because the shape was right: a Uruguayan Lerena woman married to an ARGENTINE in the decade this archive cares about. She is born 4 NOVEMBER 1880 in the Departamento de SAN JOSE, daughter of ALBERTO LERENA and MARIA INES LARRIERA; married ADOLFO CORDERO at Montevideo 28 February 1901; died there 4 January 1945. *** Nothing touches Pablo Armando. *** But her father ALBERTO LERENA, fathering a daughter in 1880, would be the right age to be ALBERTO OCTAVIO LERENA LENGUAS, born Montevideo 1850 and a grandson of Sancho - *** NOT MERGED, because a forename and an age is exactly the evidence that produced the two Arturos. ***

column1: Catedral Nuestra Senora del Rosario - Confirmation Records, DGS 4531018 item 1, images 5-80
column2: *** READ END TO END FOR PABLO ARMANDO, AND HE IS NOT IN IT. *** Seventy-six images, the complete section from the first register leaf - "Siguen las confirmaciones en la Iglesia del Sagrario (15 MAYO DE 1885)" - to the 1897 section under Bishop Gelabert y Crespo. About TWO AND A HALF THOUSAND children, *** every entry naming BOTH PARENTS *** in the form "NOMBRE de N anos hijo legitimo de PADRE y MADRE". *** NO LERENA under any of seven spellings. *** Pablo Armando was three when the register opens and fifteen when it closes, and children appear at every age from two to fifteen - so his whole plausible window lies inside the pages read. *** THE STRONGEST NEGATIVE THIS ARCHIVE HAS PRODUCED ON ROSARIO, and an independent one: the baptism indexes were already read end to end for 1731-1901. *** Not read: images 81-148 (1897-1904), and any confirmations of 1883-84. Two false positives were opened and dismissed, and SEVEN images returned an empty transcript on the first pass and read clean on retry - an empty transcript is "not read", not "no Lerena".
column4: PRIMARY - full-text transcripts read, page by page

column1: FamilySearch browse - the FIVE FILMED PARISHES OF ROSARIO
column2: *** THIS ARCHIVE HAD READ ONE OF FIVE. *** All seventeen Rosario films it holds belong to catalogue 208788, NUESTRA SENORA DEL ROSARIO - the index sweeps of 1731-1901, the three-year baptism sweep and the confirmations are all one parish. The collection also films INMACULADA CONCEPCION (from 1899), SAGRADO CORAZON DE JESUS (1896), SAN JOSE (1899) and SANTA ROSA DE LIMA (1888). *** THE FINDING CUTS BOTH WAYS. It STRENGTHENS the baptism null: four of the five have no register reaching February 1882, so the Catedral was the only parish in Rosario that could hold his baptism, and reading its index end to end was the right thing to have done. *** But it OPENS a real new source: *** SANTA ROSA DE LIMA, CONFIRMACIONES 1890-1897, DGS 004581639, 141 images, transcribed in full text and never opened here *** - rounds in July 1890, Sept-Oct 1891 and May 1897 under Bishop JUAN CAGLIERO, when Pablo Armando was eight, nine and fifteen. The register's own index page carries the words "PAGES MISSING", which must qualify any null taken from it.
column4: REFERENCE - catalogue structure read; the new film not yet read

column1: 1921 Census of England & Wales (findmypast, exclusive)
column2: *** THE LAST CENSUS OF THE TAYLOR GENERATION, read 14 Sep 2026 on the day before the trial expired. *** Not on FamilySearch at any price, and the 1931 returns burned. Two households found. *** FORE STREET, NORTHAM: *** Henry Dalling, 40, INSURANCE AGENT for the PEARL (a gardener in 1911); Isabel Temple, 45; RONALD WILLIAM, 18, motor mechanic; SYLVIA MAY, 10; EDITH MAY, 8 - and *** KATHLEEN GEORGINA, sister-in-law, 50, occupation "HOME INVALID". *** That answers a question this archive had asked twice: the eldest of the ten never married, and the census says why. *** 5 KINGSLEY TERRACE, BIDEFORD: *** Henry Albert Burton, 45, ASSURANCE AGENT for the PRUDENTIAL; Irene, 42; Charles William, 13; two boarders. Two brothers-in-law in the same trade. *** TWO TRAPS RECORDED: the index calls Kathleen "DALLING" because the enumerator wrote the household surname on every line - the same shape that cost a retraction over the 1895 Buenos Aires census - and Irene's birthplace is given as BERMONDSEY, her husband's, because he filled the form. ***
column4: PRIMARY - transcripts read; original images not opened

column1: The 1939 Register (findmypast) - 26 Fore Street, Northam, schedule 98
column2: *** ITS STRENGTH IS THE EXACT DATE OF BIRTH, and it gave three. *** HENRY DALLING born 9 OCTOBER 1880; ISABELLA T DALLING born 10 SEPTEMBER 1874 - this archive had only "1874" from a tree; and *** KATHLEEN G TAYLOR born 4 NOVEMBER 1870, *** confirming the archive's date to the day and with it the reading that she and William John were twins. *** Kathleen's occupation is "INCAPACITATED" *** - the 1921 "Home Invalid" again, eighteen years on. She died five months after this register, on 29 February 1940. *** THREE RECORDS, TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS, ONE HOUSE: single at 41 in 1911, home invalid at 50, incapacitated at 68 - always in her sister's household, the eldest of ten and the only one who never left. *** Her marital status column is left BLANK where the others read Married and Single; recorded as blank, not read as single. Ref RG101/6826D/008/16, letter code WFSE.

column1: British and Irish Newspapers (findmypast / British Newspaper Archive)
column2: *** TESTED ON THIS FAMILY AND IT DOES NOT WORK - nothing found, and the reasons matter more than the result. *** "Lerena" returns 1,344 articles and the surname is DROWNED BY THREE SOURCES OF NOISE: the *** NISSAN SERENA *** motor car, advertised through the 1990s and OCR'd as "lERENA"; *** "GUTTA SERENA" ***, the old medical term for blindness, in infirmary tables from the 1750s; and *** DON PEDRO LOPEZ DE LERENA, Spanish Minister of Finance under Charles III ***, reported from the London Gazette in the 1780s - a real Lerena and not ours. Exact-keyword matching does not help, because the OCR text literally contains the string. "Mary Septima" (26), "Septima Taylor" (12) and "Lerena + Northam" (2) all returned nothing of ours. *** THE ONE LIVE SEAM IS REACHED BY SUBJECT, NOT BY NAME: "Argentine Stud Book" returns 13 genuine articles including SPORTING LIFE of 28 October 1909 on Argentine racing *** - the years Gilberto Lerena was co-founding that book. A targeted read of Sporting Life 1905-1920 is a reading task, not a search task.
column4: SECONDARY - a controlled negative, with the noise sources named
